description: The twelve-month aggregate cap, evaluated with the document's own vocabulary supplied (unit MONTHS, basis FEES_PAID, scope AGGREGATE — each taken verbatim from the clause) but with NO preferred value. Every comparability gate passes and the engine still refuses to conclude, because the acceptance position is absent. This is the fixture that demonstrates exactly what remains blocked: the engine is correct and complete here, and the missing input is the owner's.

A real cap whose period was left blank in the executed template: liability 'shall not exceed the total fees paid by Customer in the ____ months preceding the claim'. A cap phrase and a unit are present, the magnitude is not. 45C.19 makes a bare quantifier insufficient, so this is UNABLE_TO_EVALUATE and never a guess at the intended number.

Two clauses of one agreement both purport to cap Leapswitch's total aggregate liability, on different terms: 17.2 six months of fees for the affected Services, 17.7 an unfilled number of months of total fees. 45C.2 makes same-scope incompatibility CONFLICT, and both evidence references are retained. 17.2 opens 'Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement' — in-document precedence language, which 45C.27 requires be detected and reported but NEVER applied. No configured precedence rule exists, so the engine does not pick a winner. Which clause governs is a legal question this fixture deliberately does not answer. OWNER RULING 2026-08-18: this one-scope reading is confirmed — the two clauses contradict rather than stacking, so CONFLICT is the ratified expectation and not merely the available one.

source_clause: 13 Limitation of Liability, cap plus the three closing carve-outs
description: The twelve-month cap together with the clause's own carve-outs: 'Nothing in these Terms shall limit or exclude liability for: (a) death or personal injury caused by negligence; (b) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; or (c) any liability that cannot be limited or excluded under applicable law.' Each carve-out is liability that is NOT limited, so each is UNLIMITED for its own scope and no further. Four Evaluations are produced, never one flattened position, and 45C.4 is asserted: the whole provision is NOT classified UNLIMITED merely because a carve-out is. The general scope fails closed for want of a preferred value; the roll-up is UNABLE_TO_EVALUATE because Tier 1 dominates.

source_clause: 17.2, measured against the basis used in 17.7
description: Two bases appear in one agreement and they are not the same thing: 17.2 caps at 'the total amount actually paid ... for the specific Services giving rise to the claim', while 17.7 caps at 'the total fees paid by Customer'. The restriction to the affected Services is in the words, not inferred. 45B.4 forbids assuming equivalence between bases and 45C.23 forbids silent conversion, so with no configured conversion rule this is UNABLE_TO_EVALUATE rather than a comparison of two numbers that measure different quantities.

Carve-out splitting in a second, independently drafted provision. 17.3 states 'The foregoing limitations shall not apply to the Customer's indemnity obligations ... the Customer's breach of payment obligations, or damages resulting from the Customer's fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence.' Three carve-out scopes are preserved separately from the general cap, which here fails closed on basis comparability rather than on a missing preferred value — a different branch from DOC-LIAB-05, reached from different real text.

description: A real liability provision that excludes categories of damages and states no monetary cap at all: 'In no event shall CloudPe ... be liable for any special, incidental, indirect or consequential or other damages of any kind'.
